name: Faded Orange
lede: Faded Orange pairs the modifier "faded" with plain orange, naming a dulled, warm orange that Ridgway's 1912 dictionary lists a close hue for decades before the exact compound name.

sections.title: A modifier on orange, with an earlier hue
sections.body: Faded Orange pairs "faded" with [[orange]], the xkcd 2010 color-naming survey's term for this dulled, warm orange [1]. Our color library also ties the hue to Ridgway's 1912 "Color Standards and Color Nomenclature," plate XV, hue 13′ [1]. Its nearest named look-alikes are [[mars]], [[mikado-orange]] and [[ochraceous-orange]] [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this orange in 0.3 percent of the 23,781 paintings we have, 71 of them, as photographed; the within-painting lens finds it in 74 [2]. That is more common than 55 percent of the named colors in our archive [2]. It peaks in the 1900s, 1.8 times the expected rate for that century, on 11 paintings [2]. Inside a painting it most often plays an accent, in 82 percent of the 74 paintings where it appears [2]. India is the most over-represented country for it, 3.3 times the expected rate, 9 of 721 paintings [2]. The earliest match in our archive is dated 1333, nearly six centuries before Ridgway's 1912 plate; the archive's early centuries are thin, so this is a floor, not a first [2].
